text:
Predicates:
InYelpRecommendations(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
NegativeReviews(x) ::: x has received many negative reviews.
RatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Store(x) ::: x is a store.

Premises:
∀x (InYelpRecommendations(x) → ¬NegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (RatingGreaterThanFour(x) → InYelpRecommendations(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ NegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → RatingGreaterThanFour(x)) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Store(hamdenSubway) ∧ (RatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenSubway) ∨ PopularAmongLocals(hamdenSubway)) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
((ProvidesTakeOut(hamdenSubway) ∧ NegativeReviews(hamdenSubway)) → (RatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenSubway) ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(hamdenSubway)))
